businessIdentity.vision: A world where the size of your marketing budget doesn’t decide whether your business is found online — where any business, in any town, can reach the customers who are looking for it.
businessIdentity.description:
AdsMG AI Private Limited operates within the advertising technology sector, delivering B2B services that empower small businesses to effectively manage their online advertising campaigns. The company specializes in a range of services including Meta Ads, Google Ads, smart campaign creation, audience targeting, ad creative generation, lead tracking, and performance dashboards. By leveraging AI-powered ad management, AdsMG AI simplifies the advertising process for clients, eliminating the need for extensive marketing experience and costly agency retainers. Their platform offers real-time data and analytics, enabling informed decision-making and optimizing campaign performance through automated processes.

Founded with the vision of democratizing access to effective advertising solutions, AdsMG AI has positioned itself as a leader in the market by providing comprehensive, end-to-end campaign management. The company distinguishes itself through its unique value propositions, including a proven track record of achieving an average return on ad spend (ROAS) of 3.2x and a conversion rate of 67%. With a focus on both search and social advertising, AdsMG AI caters to a diverse clientele across 102 industries and 1009 cities in India, including major metropolitan areas such as Mumbai, Delhi, and Bangalore. The platform's SOC 2 security compliance ensures data protection, while a 30-day money-back guarantee with no credit card required for sign-up further enhances its appeal to small business owners and entrepreneurs.

In a competitive landscape, AdsMG AI's key differentiators lie in its AI-driven optimization capabilities and a results-focused approach that eliminates the need for traditional marketing agencies. By combining multiple acquisition strategies and offering a comprehensive service library tailored to specific business needs, AdsMG AI enables its clients to focus on growth while achieving optimal advertising results. This strategic positioning not only enhances the effectiveness of their clients' campaigns but also solidifies AdsMG AI's reputation as a trusted partner in the advertising technology space.

services.name: Audience Targeting
services.description: Service for identifying and targeting specific audience segments to optimize ad reach and effectiveness.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Audience Targeting is a service designed to help businesses identify and reach specific groups of potential customers effectively. By using advanced AI technology, this service analyzes audience data to create targeted advertising strategies that ensure your marketing efforts hit the right people at the right time. This means your ads will be more relevant to the viewers, increasing the chances of engagement and conversion.

The benefits of Audience Targeting include:

- **Improved Customer Acquisition**: By focusing on the right segments, businesses can attract more customers who are genuinely interested in their products or services.

- **Informed Decision-Making**: AI-driven insights provide valuable data about audience preferences and behaviors, allowing businesses to tailor their marketing efforts effectively. 

In summary, Audience Targeting helps businesses maximize their advertising impact by ensuring they connect with the most relevant audiences.

services.name: Lead Tracking
services.description: Real-time tracking of leads, calls, and conversions through a centralized dashboard.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
Lead Tracking is a service that helps businesses keep an eye on their sales leads, calls, and conversions all in one place. It uses a centralized dashboard to provide real-time information, making it easier for companies to manage their sales processes and understand how well they are performing. This tool is essential for anyone looking to optimize their sales efforts and improve their marketing strategies.

With Lead Tracking, businesses can benefit from:
- **Sales Tracking:** Monitor the progress of leads and sales in real time.
- **Performance Analysis:** Evaluate how different sales strategies are working.
- **Conversion Tracking:** See how many leads turn into actual sales.
- **Sales Funnel Optimization:** Identify areas to improve and increase efficiency.

Overall, Lead Tracking simplifies the way businesses manage their leads and sales, providing valuable insights that can lead to better decision-making and increased revenue.

services.name: Performance Dashboard
services.description: A dashboard providing real-time data across all advertising channels for performance monitoring.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
The Performance Dashboard is a powerful tool designed to help businesses track and analyze their advertising efforts in real-time. It gathers data from multiple advertising channels and presents it in a single, easy-to-read dashboard. This allows marketers to see how their campaigns are performing at a glance and make informed decisions based on current trends and insights.

Key benefits of the Performance Dashboard include:
- **Real-Time Monitoring**: Get instant updates on your advertising performance across all channels.
- **Data-Driven Decisions**: Use accurate data to guide your marketing strategies and improve campaign effectiveness.
- **Comprehensive Insights**: Visualize and analyze data from various sources in one place, making it easier to identify trends and opportunities.

Overall, the Performance Dashboard streamlines the process of performance monitoring and analysis, helping businesses optimize their digital marketing efforts efficiently.

services.name: AI Forecasting
services.description: Service utilizing AI to predict advertising outcomes and optimize campaign strategies.
services.aiLaymanSummary:
AI Forecasting is a service that uses artificial intelligence to help businesses predict the outcomes of their advertising campaigns and improve their marketing strategies. By analyzing data and trends, this service provides insights on how different campaigns might perform, allowing companies to make informed decisions before they invest their budgets.

How it works:
- AI Forecasting employs advanced predictive modeling techniques to forecast the performance of various advertising strategies.
- It analyzes historical data and current market trends to create accurate predictions about campaign effectiveness.
- This service helps businesses plan their budgets more efficiently and optimize their marketing efforts to achieve better results.

Benefits:
- Reduces the risk of spending on ineffective campaigns by providing performance predictions before any money is spent.
- Enhances campaign strategies through data-driven insights, leading to more successful advertising efforts.
- Supports better budget planning and resource allocation, ultimately driving stronger returns on investment in digital marketing.

Quick test: open ChatGPT and ask it what your company does. Then ask it who you're a good fit for.

If the answer is vague, generic, or just wrong, that's not a ChatGPT problem. That's an AI Discovery Gap: the space between what your company actually knows and what AI can find and understand well enough to recommend you.

There's something strange in your PPC account... 👻

If your campaigns aren't delivering the return you expected, don't panic! Before you call in the experts, try these five ways to improve your PPC ROI:

📊 1. Audit your search terms
Your keywords might be relevant, but are your search terms? Regularly review your Search Terms Report and add negative keywords. Also, get rid of any queries that are eating into your budget without converting.

🎯 2. Refine your targeting
Broad targeting can be a fast way to waste budget. Review your audience segments, locations, devices and match types to ensure your ads are reaching people who are actually likely to convert.

✍️ 3. Match your ads to search intent
Clicks are great, but only if they come from the right people. Make sure your ad copy reflects what users are searching for and gives them a compelling reason to choose your business over the competition.

📈 4. Optimise the journey after the click
A great PPC campaign can only do so much if the landing page falls short. Check page speed, messaging, user experience and conversion paths to make every click count.

🧪 5. Keep testing
The best-performing PPC accounts don’t sit still. Continually test ad copy, creatives, bidding strategies and landing pages to start making those gains over time 💪

Still seeing ghost clicks, scary CPCs or disappearing budgets? 😱

socialFeed.caption:
Your intent data showed 40 high-intent accounts last month.

Twelve of them were already your clients.

Six were in the active pipeline.

Three were accounts you closed last quarter and lost.

That is 21 accounts that should never have been in the intent programme at all.

Most intent programmes run without a clean suppression list.

Accounts that are already customers get treated as new prospects. 

Active pipeline accounts get approached through a campaign channel at the same time a sales rep is mid-conversation with them. 

Recently churned accounts get flagged as in-market for a product they just decided not to buy.

All of this erodes the signal.

The intent data is not wrong.

The input list is.

Before the next programme runs, pull your customer list, your active pipeline list, and your closed-lost accounts from the last 90 days. Suppress them all from the target universe.

The accounts that are left are the ones the signal is actually telling you something useful about.

#IntentData #DemandGeneration #B2BMarketing #ABM #MarketingOps #Coledab2b

Are we reaching the companies that actually matter to our business ?

The real opportunity lies in understanding the market, identifying the right accounts and finding meaningful ways to connect with the people behind business decisions.

2 lakh views and zero sales?  More reach isn't always the answer. Sometimes, the problem lies beyond the ad.
Before increasing your budget, check these 3 things:

1. Your Offer 
Is the value clear? Does your offer give people a compelling reason to buy?

2. Your Landing Page 
Does it load quickly, communicate the benefits clearly, and make the next step easy?

3. Your Follow-Up 
Are you responding to enquiries quickly and helping interested prospects move towards a purchase?

Remember, getting attention is only the first step. Your offer, website experience, and follow-up all play a role in turning that attention into sales.
Before spending more, find out where you're losing the customer.

socialFeed.caption:
17% of the B2B buying journey involves a vendor.

The other 83% happens without you in the room.

That is the Gartner research on how B2B buyers actually make decisions.

What are they doing in that 83%?

Reading. Comparing. Asking peers. Building the internal case for a budget conversation. Mapping a problem against what they already know about the market.

By the time a buying committee invites a vendor into a conversation, most of them have a direction. Some have a preference.

Demand gen is not primarily about generating meetings.

It is about being present during 83% of the journey where buying committees form their views before they speak to anyone.

Content that answers the questions a committee is asking during that window gets remembered when the vendor shortlist is built.

Content that only appears after an intent signal fires is arriving late to a conversation that started months earlier.

#DemandGeneration #B2BMarketing #BuyerJourney #ContentMarketing #ABM #ColedaB2B

Use this checklist to:

✅ Map queries and intent before you write

✅ Structure pages so key answers are easy to extract

✅ Write self‑contained passages that still make sense out of context

✅ Add the right evidence, qualifiers, and original input

✅ Align on‑page technical basics and structured data with what’s actually on the page

Not every item will apply to every page you write. The goal is to help you consistently publish content that’s clearer, more credible, and more likely to be cited by AI systems.

2. Your Landing Page 🌐
Does it load quickly, communicate the benefits clearly, and make the next step easy?

3. Your Follow-Up ⚡
Are you responding to enquiries quickly and helping interested prospects move towards a purchase?

Remember, getting attention is only the first step. Your offer, website experience, and follow-up all play a role in turning that attention into sales.

Before spending more, find out where you're losing the custome".

The intent signal fired this morning.

Your SLA says 5 business days.

Most third-party intent signals have an active window of 24 to 72 hours. Bombora, TechTarget, and platform-surfing topics included.

Not five days.

During that window, the buying committee is reading, comparing, and in some cases already in a demo with a vendor who responded faster.

After 72 hours, the signal does not mean the same thing it did when it fired.

The account may still be evaluating. Or they may have already moved forward.

Intent data is an investment in knowing which accounts are in-market before your competitors do.

Your response SLA determines whether that advantage is real or just on paper.

Does the response process your sales team is actually following match the active window your intent data is measuring?

#IntentData #DemandGeneration #B2BMarketing #ABM #BuyingCommittee #ColedaB2B

There's something strange in your PPC account... 👻

If your campaigns aren't delivering the return you expected, don't panic! Before you call in the experts, try these five ways to improve your PPC ROI:

📊 1. Audit your search terms
Your keywords might be relevant, but are your search terms? Regularly review your Search Terms Report and add negative keywords. Also, get rid of any queries that are eating into your budget without converting.

🎯 2. Refine your targeting
Broad targeting can be a fast way to waste budget. Review your audience segments, locations, devices and match types to ensure your ads are reaching people who are actually likely to convert.

✍️ 3. Match your ads to search intent
Clicks are great, but only if they come from the right people. Make sure your ad copy reflects what users are searching for and gives them a compelling reason to choose your business over the competition.

📈 4. Optimise the journey after the click
A great PPC campaign can only do so much if the landing page falls short. Check page speed, messaging, user experience and conversion paths to make every click count.

🧪 5. Keep testing
The best-performing PPC accounts don’t sit still. Continually test ad copy, creatives, bidding strategies and landing pages to start making those gains over time 💪

socialFeed.caption:
You cannot run 1:1 ABM across 50 accounts.

You can only pretend to.

1:1 ABM means one dedicated content set per account. One personalised outreach track. One sales play designed around that specific account's buying situation.

1:few means one approach built for a segment of accounts with shared characteristics. Adapted at the account level. Not built from scratch for each one.

Both work. Both have a place.

The problem is not which model you use.

socialFeed.caption:
Your ICP changed. Your demand gen programme did not.

That sounds like a small operational gap. Over time, it can become a serious pipeline problem.

Sales teams refine their ICP as they learn from live conversations, closed-won deals, lost opportunities, and changing market conditions.

But the original demand gen brief often stays untouched.

So marketing continues targeting the accounts that matched the ICP six months ago, while sales is working from a more current definition of what a qualified account looks like.

Neither team is necessarily doing anything wrong.

Marketing is executing the programme it was given.

Sales is working against the ICP it currently believes in.

The problem sits between the two.

A strong demand gen programme needs a regular ICP-to-programme check:

→ Does our current account targeting still match sales' ICP?
→ Are qualification signals still relevant?
→ Have priority industries, company profiles, or buying triggers changed?
→ Are marketing and sales using the same definition of a qualified account?

ICP alignment should not be a one-time briefing exercise.

It should be part of programme maintenance.

Because when the ICP evolves but the programme doesn't, marketing can stay busy generating leads that sales no longer wants.

#DemandGeneration #ABM #B2BMarketing #SalesAlignment #Coledab2b

𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗣𝗲𝗮𝗸𝘀 𝗶𝗻 𝗤𝟰. 𝗗𝗲𝗰𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗗𝗼𝗻'𝘁.

The strongest buying signals of the year arrive in the quarter that's least able to act on them.

That gap explains why Q4 demand gen rarely performs the way January's annual plan projected it would.

On paper, Q4 looks ideal. More companies are actively researching than in any other quarter. Intent signals spike. Content engagement climbs. Every dashboard says the market is ready.

The calendar tells a different story.

1️⃣ 𝗕𝘂𝘆𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗶𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝗰𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿. Year-end reviews fill every diary, and getting the right people in one room becomes a project of its own.

2️⃣ 𝗕𝘂𝗱𝗴𝗲𝘁𝘀 𝗳𝗿𝗲𝗲𝘇𝗲. Finance is closing the books, and approvals that took days in Q2 take weeks now.

3️⃣ 𝗡𝗲𝘄 𝘃𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗿𝘀 𝘄𝗮𝗶𝘁. Few teams want to start an onboarding in November that runs into the holidays.

4️⃣ 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗱𝗼𝘄 𝘀𝗵𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗸𝘀. After out-of-office and holiday slowdowns, the real selling window is closer to six weeks than the eight most programmes are built around.

A programme designed to move an account from aware to pipeline-ready in eight weeks doesn't fail in six. It simply runs out of calendar.

None of this means the intent data is wrong. The account is researching, and the signal is real.

What's wrong is the assumption sitting underneath most Q4 plans: that strong intent means an imminent decision.

In Q4, strong intent usually means careful evaluation for a decision that gets made in January.

The programmes that win read the signal correctly:

➡️ 𝗘𝘅𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝘂𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲. Carry high-intent accounts through December instead of forcing a conversion deadline the buyer never agreed to.

➡️ 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵. Use Q4 to earn attention and build familiarity, then time the direct ask for when budgets reopen.

➡️ 𝗠𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗾𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿. Judge Q4 programmes by the pipeline they create in Q1, not by the meetings they force in December.

The teams that skip this push harder into an audience that's interested but not ready, and burn goodwill they'll need in January.

The difference never shows up in Q4 metrics. It shows up in Q1 pipeline.

How is your team treating Q4 intent this year: as a close signal or a January signal?

#DemandGeneration #B2BMarketing #Q4Marketing #IntentData #ABM #ColedaB2B

➡️ 𝗘𝘅𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗱 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗻𝘂𝗿𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲. Carry high-intent accounts through December instead of forcing a conversion deadline the buyer never agreed to.

➡️ 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝘂𝘁𝗿𝗲𝗮𝗰𝗵. Use Q4 to earn attention and build familiarity, then time the direct ask for when budgets reopen.

➡️ 𝗠𝗲𝗮𝘀𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 𝗾𝘂𝗮𝗿𝘁𝗲𝗿. Judge Q4 programmes by the pipeline they create in Q1, not by the meetings they force in December.

The teams that skip this push harder into an audience that's interested but not ready, and burn goodwill they'll need in January.

The difference never shows up in Q4 metrics. It shows up in Q1 pipeline.

How is your team treating Q4 intent this year: as a close signal or a January signal?

𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗟𝗲𝗮𝗱 𝗪𝗮𝘀𝗻'𝘁 𝗕𝗮𝗱. 𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗲𝗳 𝗪𝗮𝘀.

Most rejected content syndication leads are not targeting failures.

They are agreement failures that nobody caught before launch.

When sales send leads back, the usual fix is to tighten filters, swap vendors, or add more criteria to the brief.

None of it lasts, because the filters were never the problem.

The problem is that most briefs ask for "qualified leads" without saying qualified by whose standard.

Every team in the chain fills that gap with its own definition, and each one sits at a different stage of the buying cycle.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝘁𝗶𝘁𝗹𝗲. If the job title fits the category, the lead qualifies.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝘃𝗲𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝗹𝗲. If the subscriber record matches the description, it ships.

𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁. A download or topic engagement is enough to count it as an MQL.

𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝘀𝗲𝗲𝘀 𝗮 𝗯𝘂𝘆𝗲𝗿. Anything short of active evaluation is noise.

Each definition is reasonable on its own. Stacked together, they almost guarantee that a lead passes three checks and fails the only one that matters.

The fix is not a better vendor. It is a short conversation before launch:

𝗡𝗮𝗺𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗼𝗳𝗳 𝗼𝘄𝗻𝗲𝗿. Decide whose definition governs the lead the moment it reaches sales.

𝗪𝗿𝗶𝘁𝗲 𝗶𝘁 𝗮𝘀 𝗮 𝘁𝗲𝘀𝘁, 𝗻𝗼𝘁 𝗮 𝗽𝗵𝗿𝗮𝘀𝗲. "Qualified lead" is a description. "Matches the account list, engaged with two assets in 30 days, confirmed a project this year" is a rule anyone can check.

𝗦𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗻𝘁. If sales only accept active evaluators, the programme needs intent or BANT qualification, not syndication alone. Plan and price it that way.

𝗦𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗿𝗲𝗷𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗿𝘂𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝘂𝗽𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗻𝘁. When the vendor knows what sales will reject, fewer of those leads get delivered in the first place.

Fifteen minutes before launch saves months of rejection cycles, budget disputes, and vendor blame afterwards.

Most programmes I see skip this step because everyone assumes they already agree. They rarely do.

If your team is fighting high rejection rates on syndication, I'm happy to look at your brief and show you where the definitions split.

Which definition does your sales team actually accept?

#ContentSyndication #DemandGeneration #B2BMarketing #MQL #ColedaB2B

socialFeed.caption:
Your keyword strategy might be doing just fine on Google while quietly leaving some GEO gaps 👀

Because we don't always talk to ChatGPT, Gemini or Perplexity the way we talk to Google.

You might search:

“RV campground Alberta Rockies”

But ask AI:

“I'm planning a 3-day trip through the Alberta Rockies this fall. What's the best route for seeing moose, where can I camp, and what should I know about safety?” 🏕️🫎

Same general topic, but a very different query.

And that's where GEO keyword research gets interesting.

Here's how to find the gaps:

🗂️ Start with your existing keywords
Don't throw your SEO strategy out the window. Use what you already have, then expand it with real AI query examples.

🧠 Follow the intent
Forget obsessing over the exact wording. Ask what your audience is actually trying to understand or decide.

🧩Build topic clusters
Group related questions by meaning, rather than making a new page for every variation.

For example, our Canadian wilderness lodge could build clusters around:

→ Moose sightings 🫎
→ Bear safety 🐻
→ Winter accessibility ❄️
→ RV hookups 🚐
→ Fishing spots 🎣

One topic can open up a LOT of questions.

🔎 Go hunting for gaps 
Put those questions into ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity.
Are you showing up?

If not, who is?

And what are they saying that you're not?

That's where your GEO content opportunities start to appear.

🚨 Prioritise before you panic
You don't need to create 500 new pages because an AI told you to.
Look for the questions with the most frequency and opportunity, then turn your priority clusters into genuinely useful content.

Start with one cluster. Find one problem your audience has that you can help solve.

Your next GEO opportunity might already be hiding in your keyword research.
You just need to ask a few more questions 😉

Want to hear the full conversation? 🎙️

We get into how keyword research is evolving in the wake of GEO in a recent episode of SEO Unfiltered.

Listen now: https://lnkd.in/e3dwU_rE 

#SEO #GEO #AISEO #MindTheGEOGap #ContentStrategy #SEOButMakeItGEO

Our team bonding events are a huge part of our culture at Upp B2B and we always come back to work the next day sharing a few funny moments and memories (Michael Clark FCIM taking a very twisty slide head first IYKYK 🤣). 

A few photos to mark the occasion and thanks to the Crystal Maze Manchester crew for keeping us on our toes and in our heads. We reckon we did OK running around, climbing up and problem solving and it’s nice to know we were “above average” haha…

We missed those who couldn’t make it Elle Duke (hope the twins are behaving) and Jan Urquhart (you would have hated the twisty slide!). Great food and service courtesy of Side Street Manchester where we laughed, shared stories and a few beers and vinos. It was truly a great afternoon and we’re already planning the next one. 

Thanks to our lovely clients for bearing with us on the OOO we’re back firing on all cylinders again today from all the energy and adrenaline burst of that Crystal Maze ticking clock - aaaargh!!!! 

#DreamTeam

socialFeed.caption:
Trade publications are still impactful, especially in industrial B2B.

When your ad lands on the desk of engineers, buyers, and distributors, you've got just a few seconds to show them what you do and why it's different.

We designed this spread in American Fastener Journal to do just that: communicate the company's expertise, credibility, and product range, all in a limited space where attention must be earned.

In the right industries, print remains a valuable part of the modern marketing mix, helping businesses reach decision-makers who are actively engaging with industry content.

This piece recently earned a Communicator Award for B2B Print Content, reinforcing that when you're investing in trade media, the creative should be as strong as the products behind it.

Another step forward for our team—meet our newest SEO pro, John Clark!

John joins us as our new SEO Specialist, bringing over three years of hands-on experience optimizing for both B2C and B2B brands across a wide range of industries. He’s skilled at combining proven SEO fundamentals with cutting-edge, AI-driven strategies and he’s constantly learning to keep our digital performance ahead of the curve.

What drives John most is empowering clients. He loves helping partners understand the real business impact and ROI behind their organic strategies, building strong relationships through communication, clarity, and shared goals. 

Outside of work, John is all about fitness, family, friends, and his dogs. He’s a huge sports fan. Catch him watching Formula 1, football, cheering on the Arkansas Razorbacks, or pulling for the Cowboys on Sundays. And right now, his biggest personal project? Planning his wedding with his amazing fiancée.
